rationale.conceptual: The method uses established ML techniques (XGBoost, simple ANN) but requires non-trivial implementation details: generating and culling RDKit molecular descriptors, stratified splitting by polymer–solvent pair, hyperparameter tuning, and careful permutation importance logic. The domain (polymer phase behavior) adds some nuance but does not require deep theory to translate into code. It is more than textbook but not a custom architecture.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves multiple stages: fetching a public dataset, extensive feature engineering with RDKit, scaling, stratified splitting, training two models (XGBoost and TensorFlow/Keras), and a leave-one-polymer-out extrapolation experiment with many small retrainings. Dependency on specific chemoinformatics tools and the need to produce two scored artifacts make it a moderately orchestrated workflow.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves implementing standard ML regression models (XGBoost, feed-forward neural network) with specific preprocessing of molecular descriptors and stratified splitting according to the paper's method. The conceptual challenge is in correctly engineering the feature vector and handling hyperparameter tuning, but no novel algorithms are required. Execution requires a multi-stage pipeline (data retrieval, RDKit descriptor computation, training two models, extrapolation analysis with repeated retraining), which is moderately complex but not excessively long.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The dataset is small (6524 rows) with moderate feature dimensions (~200); training XGBoost and a shallow neural network on this scale requires only a few GB of RAM and no GPU.
